note: The site's own collection of wishes, written for this place. Labelled honestly as a collection; new wishes are added by hand, never scraped.
wishes: I wish my grandmother could see the garden I finally grew.
I wish to learn the names of all the birds that pass over this house.
I wish the letter I never sent had been sent.
I wish for one more ordinary Tuesday with him.
I wish my hands remember how to make bread the way hers did.
I wish the sea stays exactly as wild as it is.
I wish to be less afraid of beginning again.
I wish my daughter laughs at the same jokes when she is forty.
I wish someone finds the photograph I lost in 1998.
I wish for rain on the night we plant the orchard.
I wish to hear my father's voice one more time, saying nothing important.
I wish the stray cat on our street chooses us.
I wish I could thank the stranger who pushed my car in the snow.
I wish the stars were this clear from my father's porch.
I wish to finish the song before the summer ends.
I wish my brother calls first, just once.
I wish the old oak outlives all of us.
I wish to swim in water so cold it makes me honest.
I wish the library keeps the copy with her handwriting in it.
I wish to be forgiven for the year I went quiet.
I wish my son keeps his terrible, wonderful singing voice.
I wish there is always one more page after the last page.
I wish the night train still passes at the hour I can't sleep.
I wish to hold a newborn and feel time stop being a debt.
I wish the harbour lights never learn to hurry.
I wish my mother dances at my wedding, slowly, twice.
I wish to understand one true thing about the moon.
I wish the bench by the river keeps our initials under the paint.
I wish everyone I love sleeps well tonight, all at once, everywhere.
I wish to grow old in a house with a loud kettle.
I wish the map we drew as children turns out to be accurate.
I wish I could give my younger self a warm meal and no advice.
I wish the choir down the street never disbands.
I wish for snow on the morning nobody has to drive.
I wish the last word of the story is a kind one.
I wish my garden feeds one person I will never meet.
I wish to stand somewhere with no signal and not reach for my pocket.
I wish the dog waits by the gate forever, in the good way dogs wait.
I wish to see the earth from far away and still choose it.
I wish you, reading this, get the one you are thinking of.
